sources.title: 75 Years of Odiya Film Making: A Flashback
sources.author: Kapilas Bhuyan
sources.type: Government-hosted authored IFFI retrospective; disclaimer says author views, not necessarily PIB
sources.locator: Opening paragraphs; paragraphs beginning The second Odiya film, However, the Odiya film music, and The mythological films
usable_claims: Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami’s Sita Bibah formally opened at Laxmitalkie Cinema, Puri, on 28 April 1936. The account distinguishes a completed first print on 25 March and Calcutta touring-cinema showing on 29 March.
Lalita (1949) was the second Odia film; production remained sparse until the early 1960s.
Sita Bibah contained fourteen songs sung by actors; Lalita introduced background singing, with music by Gouri Goswami and Suren Pal and lyrics by Kalicharan Pattnaik.
The retrospective identifies Manikajodi, Amada Bata, Abhinetri, Malajanha, Matira Manisha and Adina Megha as films drawn from literary works.
Prashanta Nanda’s Sesha Shrabana (1976) and Sadhu Meher’s Abhiman (1977) are singled out for drawing audiences back during a lean period.
limits: Keep all derived prose across article to at most200words; above facts should be selected, not all expanded.
The page’s nationhood terminology is misleading for1936; write linguistic province only with independent history source.
Do not use its imprecise Maya Miriga award wording or award/festival conflations. This is retrospective evidence, not contemporaneous1936 programme.

sources.title: Odisha Film Development Corporation Limited, Cuttack — Manual1
sources.locator: Date of Incorporation; opening objectives list; Kalinga Studios section
usable_claims: Incorporation and commercial operation are dated22April1976.

OFDC’s objectives included financing Odia feature films and low-cost rural/semiurban cinema houses; studio facilities for shooting, dubbing, editing, music recording and mixing; festivals and assistance to cine societies.
Kalinga Studios is described as an OFDC subsidiary providing pre- and post-production facilities.
limits: Institutional objectives are not proof every facility or programme was operating continuously.
Do not confuse OFDC incorporation1976 with a separately verified opening date for Kalinga Studios.

article_claim_groups.source_note: Il Cinema Ritrovato, [*Māyā Miriga*, 2024 programme](https://festival.ilcinemaritrovato.it/en/film/maya-miriga/), screening on 27 June; film note by Shivendra Singh Dungarpur and restoration credits. Restoration by Film Heritage Foundation at L’Immagine Ritrovata, with the director’s family. The programme credits additional technical partners and distinguishes the negative from the NFDC–NFAI print.

Kapilas Bhuyan, [“75 Years of Odiya Film Making: A Flashback”](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=67399), IFFI retrospective hosted by PIB, 22 November 2010. Opening chronology, music and literary-adaptation paragraphs. An authored retrospective, not a surviving 1936 screening programme.

[Gour–Parbati filmography](https://www.gourparbati.com/filmography.php), compiled by Khirod Naik and Shekhar Barman. Entries distinguish production from directing and identify the collective directing credit “Siddharth.”
Gour–Parbati archive, [*Chha Mana Atha Guntha* (1986)](https://www.gourparbati.com/movie_chha_mana_atha_guntha.php), story, direction, screenplay and cast credits.

Odisha Film Development Corporation, [RTI Manual 1](https://rtiodisha.gov.in/Pages/printManual/section_id:2/office_id:1345/lang), incorporation date and objectives. Institutional remit is not a claim that every service operated continuously.

Directorate of Film Festivals, [31st National Film Awards catalogue](https://www.dff.nic.in/images/Documents/86_31stNfacatalogue.pdf), Second Best Feature Film citation: films of 1983, awards in 1984. Indexed catalogue text inspected; direct PDF access was intermittent.
Semaine de la Critique, [*Maya Miriga*, 1984](https://www.semainedelacritique.com/en/edition/1984/movie/maya-miriga), official selection record.

International Film Festival Mannheim–Heidelberg, [1984 archive](https://www.iffmh.de/festival/history/1984/index_eng.html), award list. The historical Third World competition category is reproduced to avoid conflation with the overall prize.

[29th National Film Awards catalogue](https://nfaindia.org/images/pdf/29th%20National%20Film%20Award%20Catalogue.pdf), Best Oriya Film citation for 1981; and [Indian Panorama 1985 catalogue](https://dff.nic.in/images/Documents/139_IPCatalogue1985.pdf), Manmohan Mahapatra biography naming Paris and Montreal screenings. Indexed original catalogue text; exact first Panorama-selection year is not asserted.

Ashok Palit, [“The New Wave Cinema of Odisha”](https://fipresci-india.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/11.-Article-Ashok-Palit-New-Wave-Cinema-of-Odisha.pdf), *E-CineIndia*, October–December 2024, pp.3–4 and 6. Used for attributed critical descriptions, not as a substitute for festival award registers.

[70th National Film Awards catalogue](https://nfaindia.org/images/pdf/70th%20National%20Film%20Award%20Catalogue.pdf), printed p.036, Sabyasachi Mohapatra biography: 1989, Sambalpuri, Gijón International Jury Award. Indexed official catalogue text inspected; the original Gijón award record and exact prize year remain unverified. The research prompt included [_rohitmahanand’s Instagram reel](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DduwFPqzOqP/); it is a discovery lead, not independent award evidence.

Riyan Ramanath V, [“Film highlights struggle to survive in rural Odisha”](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/bhubaneswar/film-highlights-struggle-to-survive-in-rural-odisha/articleshow/17396785.cms), *The Times of India*, 28 November 2012, paragraphs on *Bhukha*’s play source and folk drummers. Used for those details only; the report’s relative-year arithmetic is inconsistent and is not adopted.

Directorate of Film Festivals, [Indian Panorama 2014 catalogue](https://dff.nic.in/images/Documents/20_IPCatalogue2014.pdf), printed p.031, producer biography recording *Sala Budha*’s 2013 Panorama selection.

PIB, [62nd National Film Awards results](https://www.pib.gov.in/newsite/erelcontent.aspx?lang=2&reg=48&relid=117636), 24 March 2015, Best Odiya Film category for 2014. Language-category wording follows the award record.

Amrit Amlan Pattanaik, [“Reading auteurship and subregional subjectivities in the Sambalpuri cinema of Sabyasachi Mohapatra”](https://intellectdiscover.com/content/journals/10.1386/safm_00105_1), *Studies in South Asian Film & Media* 17(2), pp.153–172. Issue dated December 2025; publisher lists online publication on 27 March 2026. Abstract and bibliography inspected; the full article was not available in this pass.

Directorate of Film Festivals, [22nd National Film Awards catalogue](https://www.dff.nic.in/images/Documents/94_22ndNfacatalogue.pdf), Best Actor citation for Sadhu Meher in *Ankur*, films of 1974. Indexed original citation inspected; direct PDF retrieval timed out.

Nandita Das, [“I am still searching for a place to call home”](https://openthemagazine.com/art-culture/i-am-still-searching-for-a-place-to-call-home/), *Open*, 2013. Reuses the KB source identity `creators-nandita-roots`.

Festival de Cannes, [Nandita Das](https://www.festival-cannes.com/en/p/nandita-das/), official jury and film-selection history. See also the existing KB source `creators-manto-cannes` for the film’s own credits.

Akashvani, [Uttam Mohanty obituary](https://newsonair.gov.in/legendary-odia-actor-uttam-mohanty-passes-away-at-66/), 28 February 2025, cross-language film work. Career totals and disputed birth-year arithmetic are not required here.

PIB, [69th National Film Awards results](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1951758&lang=2&reg=48), 24 August 2023, Best Odia Film for 2021. The [CBFC 2021 certification list](https://cbfcindia.gov.in/cbfcAdmin/assets/pdf/Films_certified_2021.pdf), row 53, dates certification to 29 December 2021; this is separate from theatrical release.

PIB, [70th National Film Awards results](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2045960&lang=2&reg=48), 16 August 2024, Best Odia Film for 2022. This is the Odia film *Daman*, not the unrelated Hindi film of 2001.
